standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter together with the group-theoretic input used by the author: the group algebra of a finite group of order prime to l is a product of matrix algebras over the residue ring, so its modules admit filtrations with successive quotients induced from simple modules of the group

core_obligations: Translate to a representation (proof lines 10491-10505): choosing a geometric point, the sheaf F corresponds to a finite Lambda-module with continuous action of the fundamental group, and the author examines the action through a finite quotient of order prime to l.
Choose the cover (proof lines 10505-10518): using the classification, the author produces a finite etale morphism f : T -> S of degree prime to l realising that quotient.

Produce the filtration (proof lines 10518-10524): over T, the pullback becomes a module over the group algebra of a finite group of order prime to l, which admits a finite filtration with successive quotients of the form M for finite Lambda-modules M.
proof_roadmap: Translate the sheaf into a finite module with continuous fundamental group action.
Choose a finite etale cover of degree prime to l realising the relevant finite quotient.
Filter the pullback using the structure of modules over the group algebra of a group of order prime to l.
difficulty_reason: The lemma generalises the filtration statement from F_l-vector spaces to finite type locally constant Lambda-modules annihilated by l^n, over an irreducible geometrically unibranch scheme: after a finite etale cover of degree prime to l the pullback admits a finite filtration with successive quotients constant sheaves attached to finite Lambda-modules (statement lines 10478-10489). The proof translates the sheaf into a module with continuous fundamental group action (proof lines 10491-10505), realises the relevant finite quotient by a cover of the required degree (proof lines 10505-10518), and filters the pullback using the structure of modules over the group algebra of a finite group of order prime to l (proof lines 10518-10524). The non-formal content is the same as in the F_l case, now with the annihilator hypothesis supplying the bounded torsion. The claim is H2: one translation plus one filtration argument.
